content.jointProblem: The collaboration would develop and test a reproducible spatial method that links Pannonia farm policy locations, including settlement-only addresses, to field-level hail intensity estimates, and would test whether the resulting hazard indicators identify portfolio segments where municipality-level hail loading under-prices exposure.

rationale.text: The researcher has produced probabilistic hail hazard maps for agricultural insurance at 1 km resolution and validated them against parcel-level crop-loss reports.

sources.quote: This study develops probabilistic hail hazard maps at 1 km resolution using a 15-year (2005–2019) archive of dual-polarisation radar data
validated against parcel-level crop loss reports provided by the insurance cooperative Vojvodina Agro-Protect covering 14,000 parcels over 2015–2019.

rationale.text: The researcher has prior insurance-sector experience zoning hail premiums for crops using radar-derived hail frequency and intensity at cadastral-parcel level.

sources.quote: сарађивао је са осигуравајућом кућом Агропрот д.о.о. из Новог Сада на пројекту зонирања премија за градобитно осигурање усева
радарски производи за процену учесталости и интензитета туче на нивоу катастарских парцела.

rationale.text: The researcher can merge sparse rain-gauge networks with radar reflectivity over the Pannonian Plain using kriging with external drift, relevant to improving field-level precipitation estimates.

sources.quote: ordinary kriging with external drift (KED) to merge hourly rain-gauge observations from 47 stations in Vojvodina with composited reflectivity data

rationale.text: The researcher has built hail-cell detection and tracking methods that fuse dual-polarisation radar with satellite infrared data, relevant to identifying narrow hail swaths.

sources.quote: cell-tracking algorithm that fuses dual-polarisation C-band radar parameters with Meteosat Second Generation SEVIRI brightness temperatures to identify hail-bearing convective cells

rationale.text: The researcher is open to joint projects with agro-insurance and risk-management companies.

sources.quote: заједнички пројекти са компанијама из области агро-осигурања и управљања ризиком

constraints.text: The available weather input is a daily MeteoVoj grid at five-kilometre resolution, not field-level hail observations.

sources.quote: We do receive daily gridded weather data from MeteoVoj d.o.o. at a five-kilometre resolution

constraints.text: Policy-to-field matching must handle settlement-only farm addresses and quantify geolocation uncertainty.

sources.quote: a large share of our farm addresses are stored only at the settlement level, not as coordinates.

constraints.text: Validation is limited to three claim years and about 1,200 geo-tagged farm policies.

sources.quote: three full claim years with geo-tagged loss data for about 1,200 farm policies

constraints.text: The company has no dedicated research unit, and its pricing and IT staff split time with operational support.

sources.quote: The company has no dedicated research unit; applied development work is carried out by a four-person pricing team and a six-person IT team

constraints.text: The method must be able to feed the pricing model automatically, not remain a manual GIS overlay.

sources.quote: turning that into something that feeds the pricing model automatically is beyond what our team can do alone

constraints.text: The researcher is available for new collaborations but work cannot start before September 2025 because of FLOODWISE-IPA field campaigns.

sources.quote: доступан је за нове сарадње, али са почетком рада не пре септембра 2025.

risks: The researcher's hail-map work used dual-polarisation radar archives and crop-loss validation, while the company currently has daily five-kilometre MeteoVoj grids and property claims; the first experiment must test this transfer gap explicitly.
The five-kilometre MeteoVoj grid may be too coarse for narrow convective hail swaths, and the researcher's material reports correlation lengths dropping to 2.1 km for intense convective cells.
Settlement-only farm addresses create geolocation uncertainty when linking policies to field-level hail intensity.
Only about 1,200 farm policies over three claim years are available, which may limit validation and reliable detection of mispriced portfolio segments.
The company has no dedicated research unit, and integration into the pricing pipeline may stall without an explicit owner in pricing and IT.
The researcher's availability is unknown beyond the notes stating that new work would not start before September 2025.
A prior collaboration produced a flood-risk mapping tool that was completed but not integrated into the pricing system, showing a risk that a prototype is not operationalised.
questions: Can the researcher confirm availability and capacity for a start after September 2025?
What hail-relevant variables, period, and update frequency does the daily five-kilometre MeteoVoj grid contain, and can higher-resolution or radar data be accessed?
How should settlement-only farm addresses be geocoded, and what location uncertainty is acceptable for pricing use?
Are the claim and validation targets farm buildings, standing crops, or both, and are the loss data comparable to the researcher's crop-loss validation experience?
Who in the company will own integration into the quarterly pricing pipeline, and what input format does the Python batch scoring process require?
Are there regulatory or explainability constraints on using new spatial hail indicators as rating factors?
